title: Why You Can't Tickle Yourself, Why Laughter Is Contagious & the 1962 Tanganyika Laughter Epidemic — Sarah-Jayne Blakemore, Wolpert & Frith's 0–300 ms Master–Slave Robotic Tickle Delay & Cerebellar Efference-Copy Cancellation, Ishiyama & Brecht's 50-kHz Rat Lateral PAG Laughter, Duchenne de Boulogne's 1862 Orbicularis Oculi Electrodes, Dunbar & Nummenmaa's [11C]Carfentanil PET Endorphin Surge Inside PIEZO2 & Human MOR–Gi (PDB 6KG7, 8EFQ, 7SBF, 8F7Q), and Rankin & Philip's 1962 Kashasha Tanganyika Laughter Outbreak (R0 = 1.52)

teenKit.tldr: Your brain uses an internal predictive software called an efference copy to cancel out the sensation of your own touch, which is why you can never tickle yourself. However, when social cues trigger your midbrain, laughter can transform into an unstoppable, highly contagious biological wave that completely overrides your conscious control.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Understanding how your nervous system filters out predictable sensations and catches emotional states helps us decode everything from the mechanics of human empathy and social contagion to severe neurological disorders.
keyTakeaways: Self-tickling is impossible because your cerebellum sends a predictive 'efference copy' to your sensory cortex to instantly cancel out the expected feeling of your own movements.

Laughter is not just a polite social reaction; it triggers a powerful endorphin surge in the brain and can spread rapidly through a group like a contagion, behaving mathematically much like an infectious disease.
Historical events like the 1962 Tanganyika laughter outbreak prove that human nervous systems can synchronize in mass social hysteria driven by genuine biological and psychological feedback loops.

vocab.meaning: A neural prediction signal sent by your motor system to your sensory processing areas to cancel out the feeling of your own actions.
The brain region at the base of your skull responsible for coordinating movement, balance, and predicting sensory outcomes.
A midbrain command center deep inside the brain that helps generate vocalizations and physical expressions of joy or distress, like rat 50-kHz chirps.
A massive flood of the brain's natural feel-good chemicals that binds to opioid receptors during high-energy social bonding activities like laughing.

quiz.question: Why does attempting to tickle yourself result in a completely flat, non-tickly sensation?
options: Your skin lacks the nerve endings required to detect your own fingers.
Your cerebellum predicts your movement and sends a signal that cancels out the expected sensory feedback.
Your brain intentionally blocks all nerve signals coming from your hands.
Self-touch triggers a massive release of pain-blocking hormones that numb the skin.
quiz.explanation: The brain anticipates what your fingers will do before they touch you and mutes the sensory response so you aren't distracted by your own movements.

quiz.question: What is the primary function of the efference-copy mechanism in the human nervous system?
options: To help the brain distinguish between sensations caused by your own actions versus sensations caused by external forces.
To transmit visual data from the eyes directly to the motor cortex.
To slow down your heart rate during periods of intense panic or anxiety.
To create contagious emotional outbreaks like mass laughter in large groups.
quiz.explanation: This predictive filter allows your nervous system to ignore self-generated 'noise' so you can pay attention to outside stimuli.

quiz.question: What does the 1962 Tanganyika laughter outbreak demonstrate about human social behavior?
options: Laughter can never last longer than a few minutes without external stimuli.
Severe stress and social isolation can completely eliminate the human capacity to laugh.
Contagious laughter can sweep through a population like a biological wave, overriding individual cognitive control.
Mass hysteria only occurs when people are exposed to specific chemical toxins in the air.
quiz.explanation: The incident showed that vocal and physical expressions of joy can act as a powerful, involuntary contagion that hijacks nervous systems across an entire community.
